info.bio:
Bauhaus es un banda de rock británica (formada en Northampton en 1978) que fue popular en los 80. La banda tomó su nombre de la escuela de diseño alemana Bauhaus, aunque en un principio se llamaron Bauhaus 1919 (año de fundación de ésta), perdiendo la última parte antes del primer año.

A pesar de que habían bandas precursoras del estilo gótico, muchos consideran a Bauhaus la primera banda en dicho estilo. Bauhaus combinaba un gran número de influencias punk y glam rock.

scenes.name: Gótico
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Término que Hannett aplicó a Joy Division y luego insulto para los epígonos, hasta que en 1982 los fans lo adoptan como estandarte frente a la excesiva luminosidad del new pop: glamour sepulcral, retorno de lo reprimido, emociones atemporales. Bauhaus («Bela Lugosi's Dead», 1979, el comienzo propiamente dicho; Peter Murphy, sex symbol heredero de Adam Ant y Bowie), The Birthday Party (el gótico americano de Nick Cave: «Release the Bats», Junkyard), Killing Joke («música de tensión», del funk de PiL a Black Sabbath, con un aura inquietante), The Cure (gótico light: Seventeen Seconds, Faith, Pornography). El club The Batcave (1982), el «positive punk», Southern Death Cult, Theatre of Hate, The Sisters of Mercy («¡Nosotros sí somos una banda de rock!»), el death rock de Los Ángeles y Kukl con Björk. Su deriva: coqueteos totalitarios y la conversión en versión postpunk del heavy metal (The Cult).

scenes.name: Dark punk y rock gótico
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk británico estuvo flanqueado desde el principio por un movimiento «gótico» que canalizaba su violencia hacia atmósferas de terror y rituales esotéricos: Stranglers, Siouxsie, X-Ray Spex. Lo más interesante evita el tono de película de terror: The Cure introducen la angustia existencial de Camus y Sartre (Pornography, Disintegration); Joy Division mezclan Doors, Kraftwerk y Black Sabbath y su final anuncia el synth-pop; Bauhaus, Killing Joke, Psychedelic Furs, los irlandeses Virgin Prunes y la cima del género, Public Image Ltd de Johnny Lydon, que convierte el punk en música de cámara con dub y ecos étnicos (Second Edition, Flowers Of Romance). Después, el gótico bailable de Sisters Of Mercy, Alien Sex Fiend, Cult, Mission e In The Nursery.

podcast.title: Band Naming - Bauhaus 1919
podcast.body: Initially, the band considered names like "The Drugs" or "Freeze." Four days before their first gig, they settled on "Bauhaus 1919," drawing inspiration from the name and founding year of a German art movement. "But four days before their first gig, they settled on Bajaos 1919, the name and year of the beginning of a German art movement."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Name Shortening - From Bauhaus 1919 to Bauhaus
podcast.body: Within a few weeks of their inaugural performance on December 31, 1978, the band decided to shorten their name from "Bauhaus 1919" to simply "Bauhaus." "Within a few weeks, their name had been shortened to just Bajaos."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Band Breakup - Hammersmith Palais (1983)
podcast.body: Bauhaus concluded their initial run with a final performance on July 5, 1983, at the Hammersmith Palais in London. The breakup was attributed to rising egos, creative differences, the pressures of touring, and Peter Murphy's severe bout of pneumonia, which forced the band to record an album without him, leading to internal divisions. "As the gig at the Hammersmith Pele came to an end, David J grabbed the mic and said, rest in peace. And that was that. Bajaos was dead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Band Reunion - 15 Years Later (1998)
podcast.body: After 15 years and four days since their last London performance, Bauhaus reunited on stage at the Hollywood Athletic Club, with thousands paying $55 US for admission. This was followed by successful gigs at the Hollywood Palladium, selling 7,000 tickets in just over 15 minutes, leading to a full reunion tour, most of which were sellouts. "15 years and four days after that last show in London, Baha's appeared on stage at the Hollywood Athletic Club."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Band Reunion - 15 Years Later (1998)
podcast.body: Fifteen years and four days after their last London show in 1983, Bauhaus reunited for a performance at the Hollywood Athletic Club, with Peter Murphy finally agreeing to a reunion after years of requests, capitalizing on the "80s retro craze." This successful gig was followed by several sellout shows at the Hollywood Palladium, where 7,000 tickets sold in just over 15 minutes, leading to a full-tilt reunion tour. "15 years and four days after that last show in London, Baha's appeared on stage at the Hollywood Athletic Club."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Crackle (1998) - Greatest Hits Compilation
podcast.body: For those interested in learning more about the band's music, a 1998 greatest hits CD called "Crackle" is recommended, noted for how well the music still sounds today. "you should pick up a comp of a 1998 greatest hit CD called Crackle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: "Sinister" Band Played at Chocolate
podcast.body: Bauhaus was among the "sinister" bands that DJ Tony Vitale "El Gitano" would play at Chocolate. This choice of music contributed to the club's reputation as the darkest and most gothic discotheque on the Ruta, attracting a clientele primarily from the punk and sinister subcultures. "Su DJ, Tony Vitale, el jitano, pinchaba bandas siniestras como Bauhaus, Cávered Volter, Othrowingister, con otras más guitarreras como The Crams o The Meteors."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: Cuando Valencia fue la capital mundial del Clubbing

podcast.title: Band Mobile
podcast.body: The group purchased a hearse from an undertaker and converted it into their official touring vehicle, affectionately naming it the "Bauhaus Mobile." "The group also bought a Hearse from a hunder taker and converted it into their official touring vehicle. They called it their Bajaus Mobile."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Birthplace and Early Support
podcast.body: Formed in the English Midlands in 1978, Bauhaus greatly benefited from the rise of small independent record labels across Britain, which provided a platform for their unique sound. "Bauhaus were born in the English Midlands in 1978 and were yet another group to benefit from the emergence of small independent record labels across Britain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 7

podcast.title: David Bowie's Advocacy
podcast.body: David Bowie became a significant fan of Bauhaus and actively lobbied for the band to be cast in his vampire movie, "The Hunger." Their performance of "Bela Lugosi's Dead" was featured in a scene filmed at the London club Heaven. "David Bowie had become a big fan and he lobbied for the band to be cast in a vampire movie he was doing called The Hunger."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Early Band Formations - Pre-Bauhaus
podcast.body: Before forming Bauhaus, the members were involved in a series of unsuccessful bands with names like This Bag Is Not A Toy, The Submerged Tenth, The Craze, and Jack Plug and The Sockets, none of which achieved significant recognition. "Before there was Bajaos, there were series of bands."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Early Formation and Naming
podcast.body: The band formed from a series of earlier projects like This Bag Is Not a Toy, The Submerged Tenth, The Craze, Jackplug, and The Sockets around 1977. They initially considered names like The Drugs or Frees before settling on Bauhaus 1919, inspired by a German art movement, four days before their first gig. Their name was shortened to just Bauhaus within a few weeks of their debut performance. "Before there was Bajaus, there were a series of bands. This bag is not a toy, the submerged tenth, the craze, jackplug, and the sockets, none of which went anywhere."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Emergence of Goth Music (Late 1970s)
podcast.body: Bauhaus is identified as a band that appeared in the late 1970s, marking the emergence of what is now known as goth music. This is significant when considering the theory that elements of proto-goth appeared earlier in the 1974 film "Phantom of the Paradise."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Theories, Thoughts, and Half-Baked Ideas

podcast.title: Final Performance
podcast.body: Bauhaus's final gig on July 5, 1983, took place at the Hammersmith Palais in London, where David J famously grabbed the microphone at the end of the show and declared, "rest in peace," signaling the band's demise. "It was one final gig. July 5th, 1983, at the Hammersmith Pele in London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: From 4AD to Beggars Banquet
podcast.body: Bauhaus, referred to as "Goth King's Bauhaus," was the sole band to transition from 4AD Records, which was initially conceived as Beggars Banquet's experimental "lab," to the parent label itself. This move exemplified Beggars Banquet's strategy of balancing experimental acts with more established groups. "Making up for the Bull Shoe was Bauhaus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 9

podcast.title: Godfathers of Goth
podcast.body: Bauhaus is often described as the "Godfathers of Goth" and was one of the founders and pioneers of the original British Goth movement. Their glamour, energy, art school sensibilities, and attitude of doom and gloom proved infectious, spreading their sound, look, and attitude globally. "The band often described as the Godfathers of Goth."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Godfathers of Goth - Enduring Influence
podcast.body: Bauhaus is widely recognized as one of the founding groups and pioneers of the original British Goth movement. Their distinctive glamour, energy, art school sensibilities, and attitude of "doom and gloom" had a profound and infectious impact globally, influencing numerous dark bands, including Nine Inch Nails, Marilyn Manson, White Zombie, Courtney Love, and The Smashing Pumpkins. "The band often described as the Godfathers of Goth."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Goth Music Emergence (Late 1970s)
podcast.body: Goth music is generally understood to have emerged in the late 1970s with bands like Baja, making the 'Phantom of the Paradise' proto-goth theory, which dates elements to 1974, notable for its earlier timeline. "what we now call goth music did not emerge until bands like Baja was appeared in the late 1970s, and death metal didn't appear into the middle 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Theories, Thoughts, and Half-Baked Ideas

podcast.title: Influence of Gothic Approach
podcast.body: Their gothic musical style, as showcased on their debut single released on Beggars Banquet, proved to be highly popular and influential in subsequent years. "Bauhaus' Gothic approach would prove to be very popular in the years ahead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 7

podcast.title: Influence on Alaska y los Pegamoides Members
podcast.body: Eduardo Benavente and Ana Curra were fascinated by Bauhaus concerts during their trips to London. This exposure influenced their personal style and contributed to the darker, gothic turn within Alaska y los Pegamoides. "quedaron fascinados con los conciertos de Killin Joke y Bout House, comenzaron a cardarse el pelo y a vestir con pantalones de piel y creepers."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: La España Siniestra ｜ La edad de oro del Postpunk y el Dark wave

podcast.title: Influence on Onda Siniestra
podcast.body: Bauhaus was among the dark-oriented bands from which Spanish "onda siniestra" groups like Parálisis Permanente drew inspiration. "De esta vertiente más oscura surgieron bandas como J-Division, Suixi and the Abansis, The Queer, Bauhaus o Killing Joke."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: La España Siniestra ｜ La edad de oro del Postpunk y el Dark wave

podcast.title: Influential 80s Band
podcast.body: Existing for barely four years and releasing just four albums, Bauhaus became one of the most influential bands of the 80s, with their work still affecting music at the dawn of the 21st century. "A group that existed for barely four years and released just four albums. But in that time, they became one of the most influential bands of the 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Internal Strife and Breakup
podcast.body: The band's progress was halted by internal issues including egos, creative differences, and touring pressures. Peter Murphy's illness with pneumonia during the recording of their next album led to the rest of the band recording "Burning from the Inside" without him, which highlighted their ability to function independently and created a "battle of egos," leading to their eventual split. "Ego's got on the way. Creative differences, the pressures of touring. And then Peter got very sick with pneumonia, just as the group was scheduled to start recording their next album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Major 90s Goth Band
podcast.body: Bauhaus was identified as one of the major Goth bands of the 1990s, a genre that emerged in the late 1970s during the post-punk era and was characterized by dark sounds and sensibilities. "The major goth bands of the 90s were Bauhaus and Suzy and the Banshee's, Sisters of Mercy, and if we go back to the very beginning we'll find that Joy Division was a major influence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 90s Part 7: The Other Genres

podcast.title: Peter Murphy's Maxell Commercial - Iconic Ad Appearance
podcast.body: In 1981, Peter Murphy was selected to appear in a TV commercial for Maxell cassettes, earning him 10,000 pounds. The iconic magazine ads based on these commercials, featuring a person in a chair being "blown away" by music, continued to be used for more than 15 years after their initial release. "The guy in the chair? That's Peter Murphy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Pioneering Goth Tag
podcast.body: The band was among the first to be labeled "Goth," largely due to their debut single, a nine-and-a-half-minute track dedicated to Bella Lugosi, the Hungarian actor famous for portraying Dracula. "Bauhaus was one of the first bands to be tagged with the Goth label, thanks mainly to their very first single, a nine and a half minute single dedicated to Bella Logosi, the Hungarian actor best known for his role as Dracula."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 7

podcast.title: Post-Breakup Projects
podcast.body: After the band Bauhaus "splintered," its members went on to form other significant groups, including Tones on Tail and Love and Rockets. Additionally, the individual members, Peter Murphy, David J, and Daniel Ash, pursued solo careers. "Bauhaus splintered into tones on tail and loving rockets and indirectly gave us Peter Murphy, David J and Daniel Ash."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Very First Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Relevance to Death Goths
podcast.body: Bauhaus is a band that is "big with" the "death Goths," who are purists faithful to the original Goth aesthetics of the late 1970s. "Baja's and Georgia Vision are big with these people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Good Goth: Part 2

podcast.title: Reunion Tour
podcast.body: Fifteen years and four days after their last London show in 1983, Bauhaus reunited for a performance at the Hollywood Athletic Club, with Peter Murphy finally agreeing to a reunion after years of requests, capitalizing on the "80s retro craze." This successful gig was followed by several sellout shows at the Hollywood Palladium, where 7,000 tickets sold in just over 15 minutes, leading to a full-tilt reunion tour. "15 years and four days after that last show in London, Baha's appeared on stage at the Hollywood Athletic Club."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus?

podcast.title: Revered Act
podcast.body: Bauhaus is mentioned as one of the bands previously discussed in shows dedicated to acts that continue to be revered and worshiped. "In the past, we've talked about bands like the Velvet Underground and the Stone Roses and Bahaus and Iggy Pop and Elvis Costello."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Smiths

podcast.title: Second Generation Goth Influence
podcast.body: Along with The Cure, The Sisters of Mercy, Siouxsie and the Banshees, and Joy Division, Bauhaus records were a significant part of "second generation Goth" in the latter half of the 1980s. "Along with the cure and the sister of mercy, choosing the banshees and some immortal Bauhaus and joy division records, there were a series of other bands that, well not exactly big in the mainstream, were huge parts of the cult of the Goth."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Good Goth: Part 2

podcast.title: The Bauhaus Mobile - Band Touring Vehicle
podcast.body: The group purchased a hearse from an undertaker and customized it into their official touring vehicle, affectionately naming it their "Bauhaus Mobile" for their travels. "The group also bought a Hearse from a Hunder taker and converted it into their official touring vehicle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: The Hunger - Vampire Movie Appearance
podcast.body: David Bowie, a significant fan of Bauhaus, successfully lobbied for the band to be cast in his 1981 vampire movie, "The Hunger." In a scene filmed in a London club ironically named Heaven, Bauhaus performs their signature song, "Bela Lugosi's Dead." "Bowie just loved what Bajaos had done with one of his old songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Bauhaus

podcast.title: Tours with Southern Death Cult
podcast.body: Bauhaus frequently toured with Southern Death Cult. "It's a band called Southern Death Cult, who often toured with Bauhaus and featured a singer who spent much of his time growing up in Southern Ontario."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Good Goth - Part 1

xref.title: Potential Proto-Goth/Death Metal Inventor (1974)
xref.body: Paul Williams' work in "Phantom of the Paradise" in 1974, particularly the "Rock Opera" within the film and the fictional band The Undead (whose singer, Peter Ebling, wore corpse paint similar to modern death/black metal), leads to a theory that he accidentally invented proto-goth or proto-death metal music. Goth music didn't widely emerge until bands like Bauhaus in the late 1970s, and death metal in the mid-1980s.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Theories, Thoughts, and Half-Baked Ideas

xref.title: The Hunger (1983) Role
xref.body: David Bowie starred as an elegant vampire in the 1983 movie *The Hunger*, which became a favorite among Goth enthusiasts. The film also featured a nightclub scene with Bauhaus performing "Bela Lugosi's Dead." "Bowie starred as a rather elegant vampire in a movie called The Hunger back in 1983."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Good Goth: Part 2

xref.title: Bauhaus Guitar Roadie
xref.body: Glenn Campling was the guitar roadie for Bauhaus before joining Daniel Ash and Kevin Haskins in their post-Bauhaus project, Tones on Tail. "Glenn Campling, the Bajaus guitar rowdy."

xref.title: Commercial Success - Beyond Bauhaus
xref.body: Love and Rockets achieved greater commercial success than Bauhaus, selling millions of records globally, headlining large tours, and securing a Top 40 hit in America. "As Love in Rockets, Daniel Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins were far more successful than Bajaos could have ever been, selling millions of records around the world, playing huge headlined tours and even having a top 40 hit in America."

xref.title: Cult Following

xref.title: Declaration at Final Bauhaus Gig
xref.body: At the conclusion of Bauhaus's final gig at the Hammersmith Palais on July 5, 1983, David J famously grabbed the microphone and declared, "rest in peace," signifying the band's official end. "As the gig at the Hammersmith Pele came to an end, David J grabbed the mic and said, rest in peace."

xref.title: Fan of Bauhaus and "The Hunger" Role
xref.body: David Bowie became a significant fan of Bauhaus due to their vampiric style and their cover of his song "Ziggy Stardust." He lobbied for the band to be cast in his vampire movie "The Hunger," where they performed "Bela Lugosi's Dead." "David Bowie had become a big fan and he lobbied for the band to be cast in a vampire movie he was doing called The Hunger."

srcs.episode: Dreampop - A History

xref.title: Joy Division – Adopted Dark Lyricism and Aesthetics Foundational to Gothic Rock
xref.body: Joy Division, along with Bauhaus and The Cure, channeled the dark aesthetic tradition from Gothic literature and cinema — filtered through 1960s precursors like The Doors — into the musical framework of gothic rock. "Joy Division and The Cure adopted dark aesthetics to help shape gothic rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Connections 3

xref.title: Major 90s Goth Band
xref.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees were identified as one of the major Goth bands of the 1990s, known for their dark sounds, introspective lyrics, and a style often inspired by Gothic novels and 1800s fashions. "The major goth bands of the 90s were Bauhaus and Suzy and the Banshee's, Sisters of Mercy, and if we go back to the very beginning we'll find that Joy Division was a major influence."

xref.body: Sisters of Mercy were identified as one of the major Goth bands of the 1990s, a genre that often incorporated elements of the occult and the bizarre, extending its culture to clubs and magazines beyond just the music. xref.title: Pneumonia and Band Division
xref.body: Peter Murphy became severely ill with pneumonia just before Bauhaus was scheduled to record their next album. This led to the rest of the band recording "Burning from the Inside" without him, a process that revealed they could work effectively independently and contributed to the internal split of Bauhaus into two factions: Peter Murphy and everyone else. "And then Peter got very sick with pneumonia, just as the group was scheduled to start recording their next album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Bauhaus Projects and Dali's Car
xref.body: After Bauhaus splintered on July 5, 1983, Peter Murphy briefly formed the band Dali's Car, which released one album before he embarked on a solo career. "Peter Murphy briefly formed a band called Dali's Car, which lasted for one album before he went solo."

xref.title: Post-Bauhaus Solo and The Sinister Ducks
xref.body: After the splintering of Bauhaus in 1983, David J initially pursued a solo career before forming a group called The Sinister Ducks, which, however, did not last for a significant period. "at first, he went solo, too. Then he formed a group called The Sinister Ducks, but they didn't last very long."

xref.title: Reconstitution as Love and Rockets
xref.body: After Tones on Tail ceased activity, the group was reconstituted under the name Love and Rockets, which featured the members of Bauhaus with the exception of singer Peter Murphy. This new iteration went on to have a successful run with multiple significant singles. "When Tons on Tale Lost Steam, the group was reconstituted under the name Love and Rockets, which was Bajaos minus singer Peter Murphy."

xref.title: Second Generation Goth Influence
xref.body: Joy Division records were a significant part of "second generation Goth" in the latter half of the 1980s, alongside bands like The Cure, The Sisters of Mercy, Siouxsie and the Banshees, and Bauhaus. "Along with the cure and the sister of mercy, choosing the banshees and some immortal Bauhaus and joy division records, there were a series of other bands that, well not exactly big in the mainstream, were huge parts of the cult of the Goth."
